thread:
morgan: Anyone seeing intermittent NCCL hangs on the us-west-2c GPU pool after last night's kernel/driver roll? A few multi-GPU jobs (6423/6429) kept stalling with ibverbs CQ errors.

ria: Yep, reproduced on two different hosts. dmesg shows repeated mlx5 SRQ/CQ failures around the time the jobs stopped. Grabbing logs now.

ria: ```
[ 3456.123456] mlx5_core 0000:af:00.0: mlx5e: cq completion error on cq 1024 seq 0x7f
[ 3456.123459] ib_core: send QP 0x1f2e failed, err -110
[ 3456.123461] mlx5_core 0000:af:00.0: SRQ overflow on srq 0x8b
```

oliver: That cluster got a kernel bump + fw update and we also adjusted MTU down from 9000->1500 for an experimental tenant yesterday. Could be SRQ sizing/driver behavior change or a UDP offload interaction (RoCEv2 uses UDP encapsulation).

sam: FWIW I saw kube-proxy/iptables touching UDP packets in the same timeframe. If the MASQUERADE/NAT path rewrites checksums for RoCEv2 it can cause devices to drop packets since HW expects valid UDP checksums.

morgan: good call. did a quick tcpdump on one node before restarting kube-proxy:
```
12:34:56.789012 IP pod1 > pod2: UDP, length 1200
12:34:56.789013 IP pod1 > pod2: UDP, length 1200, chksum 0x0000  <-- after nat/masq path
```

infra-bot: autoscaler-alert: 3 nodes in gw-pool-usw2c were cycled between 02:10-02:18 during the kernel-6.1.8-rl rollout. Tag: rollout/kernel-2026-03.

oliver: Temporary mitigation we tested on a canary node: 1) bypass conntrack for RoCE UDP ports, 2) disable GRO/GSO/TSO on the infiniband-backed interface, 3) raise socket buffers/SRQ space. Commands we used:
```bash
# bypass conntrack for RoCEv2 (UDP 4791) at prerouting
iptables -t raw -A PREROUTING -p udp --dport 4791 -j NOTRACK
iptables -t raw -A OUTPUT -p udp --dport 4791 -j NOTRACK

# system networking tweaks
sysctl -w net.core.rmem_max=268435456
sysctl -w net.core.wmem_max=268435456
sysctl -w net.core.netdev_max_backlog=300000

# disable offloads on the host NIC used for RoCE
etdev=eth_ib0
ethtool -K $etdev gro off gso off tso off
```

ria: After applying that on the canary, the same NCCL job ran for 6 hours without hitting the CQ/SRQ errors. p99 latency returned to baseline. We still need to confirm driver-level SRQ sizing is not regressing under high fanout.

sam: Long-term we should: 1) update node image to add the raw-NOTRACK rule in startup for RoCE UDP ports, 2) revert the experimental MTU change for the affected pool and run a controlled test, 3) open a support ticket with vendor for driver SRQ sizing post-kernel roll.

morgan: Agreed. I'll draft a short runbook for the canary rollout (10% nodes first) and schedule the vendor ticket. Nice catch on conntrack everyone. :thumbsup:

oliver: I'll also add a k8s node-problem-detector probe to flag if ibverbs reports CQ/SRQ errors so we can auto-evacuate pods early.

morgan: Plan set — canary changes tonight, wider roll if green. Leaving this thread open for any regressions.
